subject: Hosted API upscale: Streamline commit increase & rate-limit plan
messages:
From: Alex Gomez <alex@streamline.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Increasing monthly commit — initial ask

Hi Chloe,

We had a spike this quarter and want to discuss increasing our monthly Hosted API commit from 500M tokens to 1.2B tokens for the next 12 months. Key asks from our side:
- Confirmation of per-minute and burst rate limits at that commit level.
- Any uplift discounts for committing 12 months vs month-to-month.
- How prefix/KV caching would be handled for our conversational product (to estimate token usage).

Can you send a proposal with pricing and the expected rate-limit window? Procurement is cc'd (procurement@streamline.ai). If possible we'd like to close this before the end of the month.

Thanks,
Alex Gomez
Head of Engineering
Streamline AI
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Gomez <alex@streamline.ai>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-18T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Increasing monthly commit — initial ask

Alex —

Thanks for the note and congrats on the traffic! We can definitely support a 1.2B/month commit. I've attached a concise proposal (Streamline_Commit_Proposal_v2.pdf) that includes:
- Pricing tiers (monthly token buckets and effective $/1M tokens for 12-month commit)
- Rate-limit guidance (sustained vs burst) and recommended autoscale bump windows
- Addendum language for rollover credit and audit log exports

High-level numbers from the proposal (subject to legal/finance review):
- 1.2B tokens/month (12-month term) → 15% list discount off hosted rates; committed throughput SLA included
- Sustained throughput target: 120k tokens/min (per-tenant sustained), with a 5x burst allowance to 600k tokens/min for short windows (up to 90s)
- Per-request ceilings: 2000 tokens/request default; we can increase if you need long responses but will adjust billing granularity

Next steps I suggest: 1) quick 30-min call to confirm burst window and rollover mechanics, 2) we issue an addendum and DocuSign link, 3) you return PO and we schedule capacity provisioning (typically 5 business days for Dedicated routing knobs).

I've looped in Rishi (account lead) to confirm discounting and Ben (finance) for billing flow. I'll schedule the call for tomorrow afternoon unless you prefer a different time.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0162

Attachment: Streamline_Commit_Proposal_v2.pdf (proposal, 6 pages)
From: Alex Gomez <alex@streamline.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@streamline.ai, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-19T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Increasing monthly commit — initial ask

Chloe / Rishi —

Thanks for the quick turn. A few clarifying items from procurement/ops before we lock terms:
1) Burst behavior — can you confirm whether burst is token-based across the account or per-route? We need burst headroom to be shared across our production routes.
2) Rollover credits — we need a quarterly rollover (unused committed tokens roll over for the next quarter only), not only month-to-month. Is that acceptable?
3) Audit/export cadence — we need daily audit log exports (S3 push) for tokens and request traces for compliance stamps.
4) PO process — will your DocuSign flow accept our standard PO terms? We've attached our current PO for reference.

If we can get alignment on these items I can expedite legal signoff.

—Alex

Attachment: Streamline_PO_0422.pdf (procurement PO stub)
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Gomez <alex@streamline.ai>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-20T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Increasing monthly commit — initial ask

Alex —

Great questions. Short answers below and I've updated the addendum accordingly (redwood_hosted_addendum_v1.docx attached).

1) Burst behavior: burst allowance is account-scoped (shared across routes) by default. We expose per-route ceilings if you want tighter isolation, but for your traffic profile the shared burst pool should give you the headroom you need. Admin control plane allows you to pin critical routes with guaranteed throughput slices.

2) Rollover credits: we can support quarterly rollover (unused committed tokens from month X roll into the subsequent two-month window and must be consumed within the quarter). We've added language that unconsumed quarterly rollover expires at quarter-end.

3) Audit/export cadence: daily push to an S3 bucket is supported. We'll provide a signed S3 push agreement and an initial sample export for you to validate format (CSV + line-delimited JSON for traces).

4) PO and DocuSign: we can accept your PO via DocuSign. I'll send the DocuSign envelope once legal completes the addendum review (target EOD tomorrow).

Pricing recap (finalized for the addendum):
- 1.2B tokens/month, 12-month term: 15% discount vs list
- Option for early uplift (if you exceed 1.5B/month for two consecutive months, we auto-evaluate a capacity uplift and proposed rate adjustment)
- Included: dedicated routing priority, 99.9% availability SLA, daily audit export

Please review the attached addendum. If acceptable, reply-all with approval and Ben will issue the billing instructions. We'll then send the DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Chloe Martin
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_hosted_addendum_v1.docx (addendum for 1.2B commit)
From: Alex Gomez <alex@streamline.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@streamline.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-22T17:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Increasing monthly commit — initial ask

Chloe —

All looks good from our side. Procurement approves the quarterly rollover language and the shared burst model. Procurement confirmed DocuSign is acceptable and attached our signed PO. Please send the DocuSign envelope and we will countersign today.

One quick operational ask: once signed, can you provision the routing priority and a conservative KV cache warm-up plan so we don't see a spike in token consumption the first week after cutover? Our SRE will coordinate; I'll add contact details once the DocuSign is out.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — looking forward to getting this live.

—Alex Gomez
Head of Engineering
Streamline AI
